verses.eng: The emanations of Self-willed again squeeze the light out of Sophia. And Jesus continued again in the discourse anti said to his disciples: "It came to pass again thus: The emanations of Self-willed again oppressed Pistis Sophia in the chaos and desired to take from her her whole light; and not yet was her commandment accomplished, to lead her out of the chaos, and not yet had the command reached me through the First Mystery, to save her out of the chaos. It came to pass then, when all the material emanations of Self-willed oppressed her, that she cried out and uttered the fifth repentance, saying:

The fifth repentance of Sophia. "'1. Light of my salvation, I sing praise to you in the region of the height and again in the chaos. "'2. I sing praise to you in my hymn with which I sang praise in the height and with which I sang praise to you when I was in the chaos. Let it come into your presence, and give heed, O Light, to my repentance. "'3. For my power is filled up with darkness, and my light has gone down into the chaos. "'4. I am myself become as the rulers of the

chaos, who are gone into the darknesses below; I am become as a material body, which has no one in the height who will save it. "'5. I am become also as matters from which their power has been taken, when they are cast down into the chaos,--[matters] which you have not saved, and they are condemned utterly by your commandment. "'6. Now, therefore, have they put me into the darkness below,--in darknesses and matters which are dead and in them [is] no power. "'7. You have brought your commandment upon me and all things which you have decreed. "'8. And your spirit has withdrawn and abandoned me. And moreover by your commandment the emanations of my eon have not helped me and have hated me and separated themselves from me, and yet am I not utterly destroyed. "'9. And my light is diminished in me, and I have cried up to the light with all the light in me, and I have stretched forth my hands to you. "'10. Now, therefore, O Light, will you not accomplish your commandment in the chaos, and will not the deliverers, who come according to your commandment, arise in the darkness and come and be disciples for you'? "'11. Will they not utter the mystery of your name in the chaos? "'12. Or will they not rather utter your name in a matter of the chaos, in which you will not [yourself] purify? "'13. But I have sung praises to you, O Light, and my repentance will reach to you in the height. "'15. For they have taken my light, and I am in pain on account of the Light from the time when I was emanated. And when I had looked into the height to the Light, then I looked down below at the light-power in the chaos; I rose up and went down. "'16. Your commandment came upon me, and the terrors, which you did decree for me, have brought me into delusion. "'17. And they have surrounded me, in numbers as water, they have laid hold on me together all my time. "'18. And by your commandment you have not suffered my fellow-emanations to help me, nor have you suffered my pair to save me out of my afflictions.'
"This then is the fifth repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered in the chaos, when all the material emanations of Self-willed had continued and oppressed her."

When then Jesus had spoken these words to his disciples, he said to them: "Who has ears to hear, let him hear; and let him whose spirit seethes up in him, come forward and speak the solution of the thought of the fifth repentance of Pistis Sophia."

Payalayapawas the scribe complains. And when Jesus had finished saying these words, Payalayapawas started forward, held up and laid down the book in his hand,--for he is the scribe of all the discourses which Jesus spoke, and of all of that which he did,--Payalayapawas then came forward and said to him: "My Adanay, surely then it is not on me alone that you have enjoined to take care for the world and write down all

the discourses which we shall speak and [all we shall] do? And you have not suffered me to come forward to speak the solution of the mysteries of the repentance of Pistis Sophia. For my spirit has ofttimes seethed in me and been unloosed and constrained me to come forward and speak the solution of the repentance of Pistis Sophia; and I could not come forward because I am the scribe of all the discourses."

Jesus explains that the appointed scribes are Payalayapawas and Thaawam and Mathathayahaw. It came to pass then, when Jesus had heard Payalayapawas, that he said to him: "Hearken, Payalayapawas, blessed one, that I may discourse with you; for it is you and Thaawam and Mathathayahaw on whom it is enjoined by the First Mystery to write all the discourses which I shall speak and [all which I shall] do, and all things which you shall see. But as for you, the number of the discourses which you have to write, is so far not yet completed. When it is then completed, you are to come forward and proclaim what pleases you. Now, therefore, you three have to write down all the discourses which I shall speak and [all things which I shall] do and which you shall see, in order that you may bear witness to all things of the kingdom of heaven."

When then Jesus had said this, he said to his disciples: "Who has ears to hear, let him hear." Marayam interprets the words of Jesus concerning the three witnesses. Marayam started forward again, stepped into the midst, placed herself by Payalayapawas and said to Jesus: "My Adanay, my in-dweller of light has ears, and I am ready to hear with my power, and I have understood the word which you have spoken. Now, therefore, my Adanay, hearken that I may discourse in openness, you who have
said to us: 'Who has ears to hear, let him hear.'

Concerning the word which you have spoken to Payalayapawas: 'It is you and Thaawam and Mathathayahaw on whom it has been enjoined--to you three by the First Mystery, to write all the discourses of the kingdom of the Light and thereto to bear witness '; hearken, therefore, that I may proclaim the solution of this word. This is what your light-power prophesied aforetime through Mashah: 'By two or three witnesses shall every matter be established.' The three witnesses are Payalayapawas and Thaawam and Mathathayahaw."

And Payalayapawas answered and said to Jesus: "My Adanay, hearken that I may speak the solution of her repentance. For your power has prophesied aforetime concerning it through Dawad in the eighty-seventh Psalm, saying:

Payalayapawas interprets the fifth repentance from Psalm lxxxvii. "'1. Adanay, God of my salvation, by day and by night have I cried to you. "'2. Let my weeping come before you; incline your ear to my supplication, O Adanay. "'3. For my soul is full of evil, my life has drawn nigh to the world below. "'4. I am counted among them who have gone down into the pit; I am become as an man who has no helper. "'5. The free among the dead are as the slain who are thrown away and sleep in tombs, whom you no more remember, and they are destroyed through your hands. "'6. They have set me in a pit below, in darkness and shadow of death. "'7. Your wrath has settled down upon me and all your cares have come upon Selah. "'8. You have put away mine acquaintances far from me; they have made me a abomination for them. They have abandoned me, and I cannot go forth. "'9. My eye has become dim in my misery; I have cried to you, O Adanay, the whole day and have stretched forth my hands to you. "'10. Will you not surely work your wonders on the dead? Will not surely the physicians arise and confess you? "'11. Will they not surely proclaim your name in the tombs, "'12. And your righteousness in an land which you have forgotten? "'13. But I have cried to you, O Adanay, and my prayer shall reach you early in the morning. "15. For I am miserable, I am in sorrow from my youth up. And when I had exalted myself, I humbled myself and arose. "'16. Your angers are come upon me and your terrors have brought me into delusion. "'17. They have surrounded me as water; they have seized upon me the whole day long. "'18. My fellows have you kept far from me and my acquaintances from my misery.'
"This is then the solution of the mystery of the fifth repentance which Pistis Sophia has uttered, when she was oppressed in the chaos."

Payalayapawas is commended and continues writing. It came to pass then, when Jesus had heard Payalayapawas speak these words, that he said: Well said, Payalayapawas, beloved. Now, therefore, come, take your seat and write your portion of all the discourses which I shall speak, and [of all things which I shall] do, and of all that you shall see."

It came. to pass thereafter that Jesus continued again in the discourse and said to his disciples: "Then did Pistis Sophia cry to the Light. It forgave her sin, in that she had left her region and gone down into the darkness. She uttered the sixth repentance, saying thus:

The sixth repentance of Sophia. "'1. I have sung praises to you, O Light, in the darkness below. "'2. Hearken to my repentance, and may your light give heed to the voice of my supplication. "'3. O Light, if you think on my sin, I shall not be able to stand before you, and you will abandon me, "'4. For you, O Light, art my saviour; because of the light of your name I have had faith in you, O Light. "'5. And my power has had faith in your mystery; and moreover my power has trusted in the Light when it was among those of the height; and it has trusted in it when it was in the chaos below. "'6. Let all the powers in me trust in the Light when I am in the darkness below, and may they again trust in the Light if they come into the region of the height. "'7. For it is [the Light] which has compassion on us and delivers us; and a great saving mystery is in it. "'8. And it will save all powers out of the chaos because of my transgression. For I have left my region and am come down into the chaos.'
"Now, therefore, whose mind is exalted, let him understand."

It came to pass then, when Jesus had finished speaking these words to his disciples, that he said to them: Understand you in what manner I discourse with you?" "'2. Hearken to my voice; let your ears give heed to the voice of my supplication. "'3. O Adanay, if you heed my iniquities, who will be able to pass [the test]? "'4. For pardon is in your hands; for the sake of your name have I waited for you, O Adanay. "'6. My soul has hoped in the Adanay from the morning until the evening. Let Israel hope in the Adanay from the morning until the evening. "'7. For grace stands by the Adanay and with him is great redemption. "'8. And he will deliver Israel from all his iniquities.'

Jesus commends Anadaray. He promises that the tyrants shall be judged and consumed by the wise fire. Jesus said to him: Well said, Anadaray, blessed one. This is the solution of her repentance. Aman, amen, I say to you: I will perfect you in all mysteries of the Light and all gnoses from the interiors of the interiors to the exteriors of the exteriors, from the Ineffable down to the darkness of darknesses, from the Light of lights down to the.... of matter, from all the gods down to the demons, from all the lords down to the decans, from all the authorities down to the servitors, from the creation of men down to [that] of the wild-beasts, of the cattle and of the reptiles, in order that you may be called perfect, perfected in all fulness. Aman, amen, I say to you: In the region where I shall be in the kingdom of my Father, you will also be with me. And when the perfect number is completed, so that the Mixture shall be dissolved, I will give commandment that they bring all tyrant gods, who have not given up the purification of their light, and will give commandment to the wise fire, over which the perfect pass, to eat into those tyrants, until they give up the last purification of their light."
Marayam interprets the words of Jesus. It came to pass then, when Jesus had finished speaking these words to his disciples, that he said to them: Understand you in what manner I speak with you?"

Marayam said: "Yea, Adanay, I have understood the word which you have spoken. Concerning then the word which you have said: At the dissolution of the whole Mixture you shall take your seat on an light-power and your disciples,

that is ourselves, shall sit on the right of you, and you shall judge the tyrant gods, who have not given up the purification of their light, and the wise fire will bite into them, until they give up the last light in them,--concerning this word then your light-power prophesied aforetime through Dawad, in the eighty-first Psalm, saying:
"'Alahayam shall sit in the synagogue of the gods and try the gods.'"

The repentance of Sophia is not yet accepted. She is mocked by the aeons. Jesus continued again in the discourse and said to his disciples: "It came to pass, when Pistis Sophia had finished uttering the sixth repentance for the forgiveness of her transgression, that she turned again to the height, to see if her sins were forgiven her, and to see whether they would lead her up out of the chaos. But by commandment of the First Mystery not yet was she hearkened to, so that her sin should be forgiven and she should be led up out of the chaos. When then she had turned to the height to see whether her repentance were accepted from her, she saw all the rulers of the twelve aeons mocking at her and rejoicing over her because her repentance was not accepted from her. When then she saw that they mocked at her, she grieved exceedingly and lifted up her voice to the height in her seventh repentance, saying:

The seventh repentance of Sophia. "'1. O Light, I have lifted up my power to you, my Light. "'2. On you have I had faith. Let me not be scorned; let not the rulers of the twelve aeons, who hate me, rejoice over me. "'3. For all who have faith in you shall not be put to shame. Let them who have taken

away my power, remain in darkness; and let them not get from it any profit, but let it be taken away from them. "'4. O Light, show me your ways, and I shall be saved in them; and show me your paths, whereby I shall be saved out of the chaos. "'5. And guide me in your light, and let me know, O Light, that you are my saviour. On you will I trust the whole of my time. "'6. Give heed that you save me, O Light, for your mercy endures for ever. "'7. As to my transgression, which I have committed from the beginning in my ignorance, put it not to my account, O Light, but rather save me through your great mystery of the forgiveness of sins because of your goodness, O Light. "'8. For good and sincere is the Light. For this cause will it grant me my way, to be saved out of my transgression; "'9. And for my powers, which are diminished through the fear of the material emanations of Self-willed, will it draw near after its commandment, and will teach my powers, which are diminished because of the merciless, its gnosis. "'10. For all gnoses of the Light are saving means and are mysteries for all who seek the regions of its Inheritance and its mysteries. "'11. For the sake of the mystery of your name, O Light, forgive my transgression, for it is great. "'12. To every one who trusts in the Light it will give the mystery which suits him; "'13. And his soul will abide in the regions of the Light and his power will inherit the Treasury of the Light.

have faith in it; and the name of its mystery belongs to those who trust in it. And it will show them the region of the Inheritance, which is in the Treasury of the Light. "'15. But I have ever had faith in the Light, for it will save my feet from the bonds of the darkness. "'16. Give heed to me, O Light, and save me, for they have taken away my name from me in the chaos. "'17. Because of all the emanations my afflictions and my oppression have become exceedingly manifold. Save me out of my transgression and this darkness. "'18. And look upon the grief of my oppression and forgive my transgression. "'19. Give heed to the rulers of the twelve aeons, who have hated me through jealousy. "'20. Watch over my power and save me, and let me not remain in this darkness, for I have had faith in you. "'21. And they have made of me a great fool for having had faith in you, O Light. "'22. Now, therefore, O Light, save my powers from the emanations of Self-willed, by whom I am oppressed.'
"Now, therefore, who is sober, let him be sober."

When then Jesus had spoken this to his disciples, Thaawam came forward and said: "My Adanay, I am sober, I am plentifully sober, and my spirit is ready in me, and I rejoice exceedingly that you have revealed these words to us. But indeed I have borne with my brethren until now, so that I should not anger them; nay

rather I have borne with every one that he should come before you and speak the solution of the repentance of Pistis Sophia. Now, therefore, my Adanay, concerning the solution of the seventh repentance of Pistis Sophia your light-power has prophesied through the prophet Dawad in the twenty-fourth Psalm, thus

Thaawam interprets the seventh repentance from Psalm xxiv. "'1. O Adanay, to you have I lifted up my soul, O my God. "'2. I have abandoned myself to you; let me not be put to shame and let not mine enemies mock at me. "'3. For all who wait upon you shall not be put to shame; let them be put to shame who do iniquity without a cause. "'4. O Adanay, show me your ways and teach me your paths. "'5. Lead me in the way of your truth and teach me, for you are my God and my saviour; on you will I wait all the day long. "'6. Call to remembrance your mercies, O Adanay, and the favours of your grace, for they are from eternity. "'7. Remember not the sins of my youth and those of my ignorance. Remember me according to the fulness of your mercy because of your goodness, O Adanay. "'8. The Adanay is gracious and sincere; therefore fore will he instruct sinners in the way. "'9. He will guide the tender-hearted in the judgment and will teach the tender-hearted his ways. "'10. All the ways of the Adanay are grace and truth for them who seek his righteousness and his testimonies. "'11. For your name's sake, O Adanay, forgive me my sin, [for] it is exceedingly great. "'12. Who is the man who fears the Adanay? For him will he establish laws in the way which he has chosen. "'13. His soul will abide in good things and his seed will inherit the land. "'14. The Adanay is the strength of them who fear him; and the name of the Adanay belongs to them who fear him, to make known to them his covenant. "'15. Mine eyes are raised ever to the Adanay, for he will draw my feet out of the snare. "'16. Look down upon me and be gracious to me, for I am an only-begotten; I am wretched. "'17. The afflictions of my heart have in-creased; bring me out of my necessities. "'18. Look upon my abasement and my woe, and forgive me all my sins. "'19. Look upon mine enemies, how they have increased themselves and hated me with unjust hatred. "'20. Preserve my soul and save me; let me not be put to shame, for I have hoped on you. "'21. The simple and sincere have joined themselves to me, for I have waited on you, O Adanay. "'22. O God, deliver Israel from all his afflictions.'"

Jesus commends Thaawam. And when Jesus had heard the words of Thaawam, he said to him: Well said, Thaawam, and finely. This is the solution of the seventh repentance of Pistis Sophia. Aman, amen, I say to

you: All generations of the world shall bless you on earth, because I have revealed this to you and you have received, of my spirit and have become understanding and spiritual, understanding what I say. And hereafter will I fill you full with the whole light and the whole power of the spirit, so that you may understand from now on all which shall be said to you and which you shall see. Yet a little while and I will speak with you concerning the height without within and within without."

Jesus leads Sophia to a less confined region, but without the commandment of the First Mystery. Jesus continued again in the discourse and said to his disciples: "It came to pass then, when Pistis Sophia had uttered the seventh repentance in the chaos, that the commandment through the First Mystery had not come to me to save her and lead her up out of the chaos. Qayan of myself out of compassion without commandment I led her into a somewhat spacious region in the chaos. And when the material emanations of Self-willed had noticed that she had been led into a somewhat spacious region in the chaos, they ceased a little to oppress her, for they thought that she would be led up out of the chaos altogether. When this then took place, Pistis Sophia did not know that I was her helper; nor did she know me at all, but she continued and persisted withal singing praises to the Light of the Treasury, which she had seen aforetime and on which she had had faith, and she thought that it [ sc. the Light] also was her helper and it was the same to which she had sung praises, thinking it was the Light in truth. But as indeed she had had faith in the Light which belongs to the Treasury in truth, therefore will she be led up out

of the chaos and her repentance will be accepted from her. But the commandment of the First Mystery was not yet accomplished to accept her repentance from her. But hearken now in order that I may tell you all things which befell Pistis Sophia.

The emanations of Self-willed oppress her again. "It came to pass, when I had led her to a somewhat spacious region in the chaos, that the emanations of Self-willed ceased entirely to oppress her, thinking that she would be led up out of the chaos altogether. It came to pass then, when the emanations of Self-willed had noticed that Pistis Sophia had not been led up out the chaos, that they turned about again all together, oppressing her vehemently. Because of this then she uttered the eighth repentance, because they had not ceased to oppress her, and had turned about to oppress her to the utmost. She uttered this repentance, saying thus:

The eighth repentance of Sophia. "'1. On you, O Light, have I hoped. Leave me not in the chaos; deliver me and save me according to your gnosis. "'2. Give heed to me and save me. Be to me a saviour, O Light, and save me and lead me to your light. "'3. For you are my saviour and will lead me to you. And because of the mystery of your name lead me and give me your mystery. "'4. And you will save me from this lion-faced power, which they have laid as a snare for me, for you are my saviour. "'5. And in your hands will I lay the purification of my light; you have saved me, O Light, according to your gnosis.

keep watch over me and will not be able to lay hold of me utterly. But I have had faith in the Light. "'7. I will rejoice and will sing praises that you have had mercy upon me and have heeded and saved me from the oppression in which I was. And you will set free my power out of the chaos. "'8. And you have not left me in the hand of the lion-faced power; but you have led me into a region which is not oppressed.'"

The emanations of Self-willed cease for a time to oppress Sophia. When then Jesus had said this to his disciples, he answered again and said to them: "It came to pass then, when the lion-faced power had noticed that Pistis Sophia had not been led up altogether out of the chaos, that it came again with all the other material emanations of Self-willed, and they oppressed Pistis Sophia again. It came to pass then, when they oppressed her, that she cried out in the same repentance, saying:
